newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Nomura to fight ASC regulator charges.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Nomura to fight ASC regulator charges.

text.p: Nomura International Plc, the London-based arm of Japan's Nomura Securities Co Ltd, said on Tuesday it would defend itself against civil charges begun in the Federal Court by the Australian Securities Commission (ASC).

"Nomura International denies any wrongdoing, can see no legal basis or factual basis on which the ASC's allegations can be sustained and Nomura International will be vigorously defending itself," the company said.
The ASC told a news conference earlier on Tuesday that it had begun legal action against Nomura International over share transactions in March 1996.
The legal proceedings followed a year-long investigation into share trading on the Australian Stock Exchange and the share price index (SPI) futures contract on the Sydney Futures Exchange.

The ASC said in a statement that on March 29 last year Nomura International had unwound a large arbitrage position by allowing 12,844 current-month contracts to expire and by ordering the sale of about A$600 million of securities near the end of the day's trade.

The regulator said the activities of Nomura amounted to market manipulation, wash trading (trading as buyer and seller of the same stock without a change in beneficial ownership), misleading and deceptive conduct in connection with securities dealings, and conduct calculated to create a false or misleading appearance with respect to the price of the SPI contract.
"The transactions referred to in the ASX allegations were legitimate stock index arbitrage transactions and took place in March 1996," Nomura said.
"They did not, or will not, have any adverse impact on Nomura's financial performance," it said.
